title: Cabbage, green, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Green cabbage is a leafy cruciferous vegetable widely used in cooking. When boiled without added fat it retains most of its vitamins, minerals, and a mild, tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cabbage is one of the oldest cultivated plants, with cultivation dating back over 5,000 years.
There are more than 200 cabbage varieties, including Savoy, kale, and Brussels sprouts.
Cabbage leaves contain glucosinolates, compounds that may help protect against cancer.
It features in traditional dishes worldwide: sauerkraut in Germany, kimchi in Korea, coleslaw in the United States.
Boiling in salted water helps preserve its bright green color thanks to chlorophyll.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: A serving of cooked green cabbage provides over 100 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health; cabbage supplies a large portion of the daily need.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Minerals: potassium and calcium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance, while calcium contributes to strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked cabbage without fat contains about 25 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cabbage contains raffinose, which can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled green cabbage can be served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, or salads. It pairs well with lemon juice, garlic, dill, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cabbage in the refrigerator in a sealed bag for up to 2 weeks. Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the fridge for 3‑4 days.
